messages.subject: Using as.formula() with the reshape package cast
messages.subject_clean: Using as.formula() with the reshape package cast
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to use the "cast" function from the reshape package, where the formula is not passed in directly, but as the result of the as.formula() function.

Using reshape v. 0.7.2

I am able to properly melt() by data with:

> molten <- melt(x, id=1:2)

then I can properly cast with this:

> cast(molten, days ~ variable)

but if I try

> cast(molten, as.function("days ~ variable"))

if returns the error:

Error in check_formula(formula, varnames) :
        Formula contains variables not in list of known variables

I am not sure if the problem is with cast or as.formula()

I did confirm that:

> x <- days ~ variable

> y <- as.formula("days ~ variable")

> x==y
TRUE

messages.subject: llply performing operations with the different elements
messages.subject_clean: llply performing operations with the different elements
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Suppose I have two lists,

la = list(a=1,b=2)
lb = list(a=1:4, b= 1:4)

and I want to append the components of la to the corresponding
components of lb, so that i end up with a list,

lc =   list(a=c(1:4,1), b= c(1:4,2))

I'd like to see a syntax like this,

lc = llply(list(lb,la), c) # c is just one possible function, we could
have `+`, etc. provided the dimensions are licit

but l*ply does not allow for operations in the relevant margin for
this case.

This topic on r-help,

http://www.nabble.com/rbind-on-a-list-td23194507.html

 reminded me of a discussion from last year,

https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2008-December/183616.html

Just wondering whether the latest version of plyr had a function to
handle this?

Best wishes,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: llply performing operations with the different elements
messages.subject_clean: llply performing operations with the different elements
messages.body_plain:
Hi Baptiste,

My gut feeling is that this problem reflects a poor choice of data
structure, and is normally best dealt with upstream.  e.g. for your
case, I'd do:

la = list(a=1,b=2)
lb = list(a=1:4, b= 1:4)

lab <- list(la, lb)
ldply(lab, as.data.frame)

I think it's best to think of lists like trees (because of their
recursive nature), and I'm not completely sure how the operation you
are proposing would work in general.

This is just my gut feeling however, and I'm open to being proven
wrong, but I'd like to see a complete example where you encounter this
type of problem, where switching data structures early on wouldn't be
more of a help.

Hadley

messages.body_plain:
You may very well be right! At least with my poor example, you make a
good point. I still wonder how to provide a good answer to this topic,

http://www.nabble.com/rbind-on-a-list-td23194507.html

Here i can see how one may have to deal with two or more lists that
perhaps come from different sources and could not be cast into arrays
of data.frames. Combining them is quite a challenge, especially if
there is more than two lists. (avoiding an explicit loop would involve
some obscure mixture of lapply(seq_along(), function(ii) do.call
(...)).

So, my next example may be,

makeDF <- function(n){
	data.frame(rnorm(n), rnorm(n))
}

d1 <- list(
	a=makeDF(3),
	b=makeDF(4))

d2 <- list(
	a=makeDF(1),
	b=makeDF(5))

d3 <- list(
	a=makeDF(1),
	b=makeDF(1))

fullList <- list(d1, d2, d3)
l_ply(fullList, str)

combined <- list() # R inferno is my next stop

for(ii in seq_along(d1)){ # ideally sweep along named columns

	combined[[ii]] <- do.call(rbind, llply(fullList, "[[", ii))

}

I hope this is clearer!

Cheers,

baptiste

> l_ply(fullList, str)

Another option would be melt from the reshape package, which does a
decent job in this case (but might not in general).  Otherwise any
approach would have to follow the same basic technique that you used.
Personally, I'd break the steps up slightly differently:

extract <- function(list, name) llply(list, "[[", name)

rbind.fill(extract(fullList, "a"))
rbind.fill(extract(fullList, "b"))

Hadley

--
